subject: Acme TCO post-call recap
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Linda Huang <linda.huang@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme TCO post-call recap

Hi Sam & Linda,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — good conversation. Per our call, I wanted to recap the key pain points, goals, and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we build a detailed cost model.

Key pain points (what you told us):
- Token cost is the dominant line item for your customer-facing assistant (current spend unpredictable month-to-month).
- Burst traffic for end-of-month reports causes latency spikes and throttling.
- Need predictability for finance to include RL/LLM line in budget (monthly cap / committed spend).
- Concern about model quality when moving to aggressive quantization; want objective checks.

Goals we heard:
- Keep average generation latency < 300ms for user-facing flows; tail latency < 1s for 99th pct.
- Reduce per-token cost by 30–50% without sacrificing quality on top intents.
- Pilot in October that demonstrates cost savings and stable latency under real load.

Technical levers we discussed: token economics + batching/caching, quantization, and dedicated capacity. Quick summary:
- Batching & prefix/KV caching: can reduce effective tokens served by caching repeated prefixes and enabling continuous batching for high-concurrency endpoints.
- Quantization & model variants: moving to 4-bit quant can lower GPU token costs materially; we recommend validation against your eval prompts.
- Dedicated pools: reserved capacity for predictable tail behavior and lower per-token unit price at scale.

Requested deliverables / next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll run a high-level TCO worksheet for three scenarios (baseline, optimized caching/batching, dedicated + quantized).
2) Redwood to propose an initial pilot (4 weeks) with success criteria: <30% cost reduction or equivalent ROI and no >5% drop in top-intent accuracy.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the spreadsheet and pick pilot dates — will include infra/ops from your side.

I attached a simple modeling workbook and a short pricing options PDF to get us started.

Thanks —
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>

Cc: Linda Huang <linda.huang@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme TCO post-call recap

Rafael — thanks for the clear recap. This lines up with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Budget: finance has tentatively earmarked ~$50k/month for LLM infra for Q4 but wants a predictable cap and a clear savings plan if we move away from current vendor.
- Latency: 300ms avg is correct for interactive flows; batch reporting flows can tolerate higher latency but need predictable throughput.
- Quality bar: we will validate top 10 intents with live A/B testing during the pilot — if quality drops >5% we’ll halt the pilot.

Please include a per-1M-token cost row for each scenario (baseline, caching, quant, dedicated) and a sensitivity table for 1M / 5M / 10M tokens. If you can show a 40%+ delta in the optimized scenario we’ll present to finance.

Looping in Linda for schedule and infra alignment. Can you also include a short note on any assumed model family (e.g., LlamaX-13B quantized) and which latency numbers map to which configs?

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
sam.patel@acme.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Linda Huang <linda.huang@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme TCO post-call recap — preliminary model and next steps

Sam / Linda — appreciate the quick reply and the constraints. I’ve attached a first-pass TCO workbook (tabbed by scenario) and a short note that maps model/quantization configs to expected latency. High-level takeaways from our initial model:

- Baseline (current configuration): $1,200 per 1M tokens served (example numbers from your reported usage pattern).
- Optimized (batching + prefix/KV caching + request-level caching): $720 per 1M tokens (~40% savings).
- Dedicated + quantized (reserved GPU pool + 4-bit quantization on compatible model variant): $480 per 1M tokens (60% savings vs baseline) — dependent on validation of quality tests.

Assumptions and notes:
- The caching scenario assumes 20–30% effective token reduction on your chat flows based on repeated prefixes and shared system prompts.
- Quantization savings assume a compatible model (we recommend LlamaX-13B quantized) and that your eval set shows <5% deficit on top intents.
- Dedicated pools pricing includes a predictable monthly commit with a lower per-token unit at scale; we show 3 commit tiers in the workbook.

ROI framing: at your current run rate, moving to the optimized scenario yields a 3–4 month payback on a modest pilot if we can capture the projected token reductions in production. The dedicated + quantized path shows a sub-3 month payback if you commit to the mid-tier reserved capacity.

Proposed pilot plan (four weeks):
- Week 0: alignment & infra checks (who: Acme infra + Vivek/Marissa)
- Week 1–2: shadow traffic + A/B eval set run (measure quality & latency)
- Week 3: ramp & monitor cost; adjust batching/cache params
- Week 4: run final readout & decision to roll to prod or iterate

Next steps I’ll take this week:
1) Send a short pilot SOW draft and pricing options (attached).
2) Book a 30-min review with Sam/Linda + infra for next Tue (I’ll propose times).
3) Work with Marissa and Vivek to prepare an infra checklist for the pilot.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
- Live model mapping doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B3cRedwood-Acme-TCO

Thanks —
